rationale: A wins because it keeps every angle inside a pitchable fact pattern, especially “Bumble's AI relaunch will be judged on one number it hasn't reported yet.” B has competent bones, but “AI matchmaking just went mainstream” wanders straight into fake-trend country and then admits the needed category proof is “not supplied.” A gives the founder a usable decision tree: pick one lane, fix the reporting-date and disclosure holes, and do not sell results Bumble does not have.
gaps_in_A: “the first product the returned founder has put their name on since coming back this year” is plausible but not in the supplied facts; confirm before pitching.
“one concrete decision the founder made in the relaunch that the previous leadership would not have made” asks for a counterfactual that may be impossible unless the founder will say it on record.
gaps_in_B: “AI matchmaking just went mainstream” is an invented category trend from one company’s relaunch. That is not a trend; that is one data point wearing a trench coat.
“category-standard feature, not a novelty” is not grounded in the update and needs outside evidence before it belongs in the angle set.
“the feature and the user criticism are both live right now” overstates timing. The update says some users have criticized AI in dating, not that a live backlash is happening at relaunch.
“her first fix is AI” and “first major public move” may be true, but the update does not establish firstness. Do not decorate the timeline because the headline wants a little drama.
